To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“evaluation-based governance” is an important concept to understand the development and the future of higher education in Europe.
“good governance” in the sense of “New Public Management” is a prerequisite for the evaluation of teaching and research in higher education.
the academic profession perceives the evaluation of research in higher education as a “good thing” but that the evaluation of teaching is perceived as a “bad thing”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to govern the evaluation of research in higher education in order to enhance the performance of universities.
the following questions.
how the academic profession perceives the evaluation of research, teaching, and governance in higher education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evaluation of research is perceived as more important than the evaluation of teaching.
the academic profession perceives the evaluation of research as a “must”, but the evaluation of teaching as a “should”.

there does not seem to exist a single “New University Governance”, but rather different “New University Governance” approaches in Europe, depending on the applied dimension (indicator, indicator packages) of governance and the evaluation of research, teaching and the institution as a whole.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the “New Governance” in higher education has to be understood as a “hybrid” of different governance approaches.
the evaluation of research, and to some degree of teaching, has become a key element of university governance in Europe.
the evaluation of research is perceived by the academic profession in a different way than the evaluation of teaching.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the academic profession perceives evaluation as a “double-edged sword”.
the academic profession perceives the evaluation of research as more important than the evaluation of teaching in higher education.
there is a need for a more differentiated view of NPM and its governance approaches in higher education.
